blocks.text: Capitol Hill Houses: streets and boundaries

items.t: Capitol Hill is the hill north of Hastings Street in northwest Burnaby: its houses climb from the Hastings Corridor shopping street up toward Burrard Inlet.
Willingdon Avenue is the west anchor: Confederation Park, the McGill Library and the Eileen Dailly pool cluster sit at Willingdon Avenue and Albert Street.
Pandora Street carries two of the hill's institutions: Confederation Park Elementary at 4715 Pandora Street and the Capitol Hill Children's Centre at 5750 Pandora Street.

blocks.text: Capitol Hill Houses: the housing stock

items.t: Houses on the hill sit behind a low-rise main street: the City's land use framework pairs the walkable Hastings Corridor with the residential streets of the Heights and Capitol Hill plan area above it.
The current zoning frame is the Burnaby Zoning Bylaw 2026, cited in the bylaw as replacing the 1965 bylaw, with R1 as the Small-Scale Multi-Unit Housing District (SSMUH).

One Hastings-fronting lot shows the transition stock: 4472 Hastings Street, a former service station site, was drawn for about 5,760 square feet of retail plus 34 strata units under a Comprehensive Development (CD) zone.

blocks.text: Capitol Hill Houses: rules that affect buyers

items.t: Small-scale multi-unit housing rules now run through the R1 district: the City's child care page confirms R1 Small-Scale Multi-Unit Housing District as a current Burnaby zoning district name.
Hastings Street itself is a study corridor: TransLink and the City are studying street improvements on Hastings Street between Boundary Road and Duthie Avenue.
Traffic rules on the hill's side streets are under active review: the City has completed a comprehensive North Burnaby Traffic Calming Study for the Burnaby Heights and Capitol Hill neighbourhood.

blocks.text: Capitol Hill Houses: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: Confederation Park's cenotaph, at the park's north end, holds a Heritage Designation and is listed on Burnaby's Community Heritage Register.
The McGill Branch library at Albert and Alpha streets sits kitty-corner to the Eileen Dailly Leisure Pool and Fitness Centre, inside the park edge.
The Confederation Community Centre for seniors, built in 1971 and expanded in 1988, is the building slated for replacement inside the deferred new complex.
Capitol Hill Children's Centre, at Capitol Hill Elementary, 5750 Pandora Street, provides 25 child care spaces and is run by the Lower Mainland Purpose Society.
The R2 Marine-Willingdon RapidBus now runs to Metrotown, giving Willingdon Avenue at Hastings a one-seat ride between the North Shore and Metrotown every 6 to 7 minutes at weekday peak.

blocks.text: Capitol Hill Houses: development and new projects

items.t: 4472 Hastings Street, Capitol Hill (4472 Hastings) Ltd. Partnership, mixed use with about 5,760 square feet of street-front retail and 34 strata units on a former service station site at Hastings Street and Willingdon Avenue.
Confederation Park Community Centre, Willingdon Avenue and Albert Street, City of Burnaby, three-level community centre replacing the seniors centre.

blocks.text: Capitol Hill Houses: getting around

items.t: The R5 Hastings Street RapidBus is the hill's trunk route: Burrard Station to SFU, listed by TransLink among its six RapidBus routes.
The R2 Marine-Willingdon RapidBus extension, launched September 7, adds a frequent all-day link from Willingdon Avenue to Park Royal and Metrotown.
Local streets on the hill were studied as one system: the North Burnaby Traffic Calming Study covered Burnaby Heights and Capitol Hill together for pedestrian, cyclist and driver safety.

blocks.text: Capitol Hill Houses: risks and due diligence

items.t: Check which zoning bylaw version applies to a rebuild: the Burnaby Zoning Bylaw 2026 (Bylaw No. 14815) renames districts, including R1 for small-scale multi-unit housing, so an old R5 or RS reference on a listing may be stale.
Check the deferred centre's effect on Albert Street plans: the Confederation Park Community Centre project is deferred, so do not price in a new facility opening beside Willingdon Avenue.

Capitol Hill home prices: what sold, November 2025 to October 2026

31 houses sold in Capitol Hill with a median price of $2,040,000 (the middle half sold between $1,646,500 and $2,380,000), taking a median of 33 days to sell at 95.5% of the last list price; 0% sold above list. They had a median $645 per square foot, a median year built of 1985 and a median lot of 4,026 square feet.

faq.q: How many houses are for sale in Capitol Hill?
faq.a: 34, in the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® month-end figures for October 2026. Listings change every day; Jared can tell you what is available now.

faq.q: Is Capitol Hill a buyers’ or sellers’ market for houses?
faq.a: With a sales ratio of 9% in October 2026, houses in Capitol Hill sat in a buyers’ market. The reports read under 12% as a buyers’ market and over 20% as a sellers’ market.

faq.q: How many houses sold in Capitol Hill from June to October 2026?
faq.a: Between June and October 2026, 14 houses sold in Capitol Hill; Burnaby as a whole recorded 251.

faq.q: What did houses in Capitol Hill sell for?
faq.a: 31 houses sold in Capitol Hill from November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026, at a median price of $2,040,000.

faq.q: How long do houses take to sell in Capitol Hill?
faq.a: Typical time on the market was 33 days. At the median, sale prices were 95.5% of list, and 0% of sales closed above list (November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026).
